17: /// A runtime value stack used during evaluation
18: ///
19: /// A note on implementation:
20: ///
21: /// We previously set up the stack in a traditional way, where stack frames had parents which would
22: /// represent other frames that you might return to when exiting a function.
23: ///
24: /// While experimenting with blocks, we found that we needed to have closure captures of variables
25: /// seen outside of the blocks, so that they blocks could be run in a way that was both thread-safe
26: /// and followed the restrictions for closures applied to iterators. The end result left us with
27: /// closure-captured single stack frames that blocks could see.
28: ///
29: /// Blocks make up the only scope and stack definition abstraction in Nushell. As a result, we were
30: /// creating closure captures at any point we wanted to have a Block value we could safely evaluate
31: /// in any context. This meant that the parents were going largely unused, with captured variables
32: /// taking their place. The end result is this, where we no longer have separate frames, but instead
33: /// use the Stack as a way of representing the local and closure-captured state.
34: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
35: pub struct Stack {
36:     /// Variables
37:     pub vars: Vec<(VarId, Value)>,
38:     /// Environment variables arranged as a stack to be able to recover values from parent scopes
39:     pub env_vars: Vec<EnvVars>,
40:     /// Tells which environment variables from engine state are hidden, per overlay.
41:     pub env_hidden: HashMap<String, HashSet<String>>,
42:     /// List of active overlays
43:     pub active_overlays: Vec<String>,
44:     pub recursion_count: u64,
45:     pub parent_stack: Option<Arc<Stack>>,
46:     /// Variables that have been deleted (this is used to hide values from parent stack lookups)
47:     pub parent_deletions: Vec<VarId>,
48:     pub(crate) out_dest: StackOutDest,
49: }

58:     /// Create a new stack.

63:     /// Use [`Stack::capture`] afterwards if you need to evaluate an expression to a [`Value`](crate::Value)
64:     /// (as opposed to a [`PipelineData`](crate::PipelineData)).

78:     /// Create a new child stack from a parent.
79:     ///
80:     /// Changes from this child can be merged back into the parent with
81:     /// [`Stack::with_changes_from_child`]
82:     pub fn with_parent(parent: Arc<Stack>) -> Stack {
83:         Stack {
84:             // here we are still cloning environment variable-related information
85:             env_vars: parent.env_vars.clone(),
86:             env_hidden: parent.env_hidden.clone(),
87:             active_overlays: parent.active_overlays.clone(),
88:             recursion_count: parent.recursion_count,
89:             vars: vec![],
90:             parent_deletions: vec![],
91:             out_dest: parent.out_dest.clone(),
92:             parent_stack: Some(parent),
93:         }
94:     }

96:     /// Take an [`Arc`] parent, and a child, and apply all the changes from a child back to the parent.
97:     ///
98:     /// Here it is assumed that `child` was created by a call to [`Stack::with_parent`] with `parent`.
99:     ///
100:     /// For this to be performant and not clone `parent`, `child` should be the only other
101:     /// referencer of `parent`.
102:     pub fn with_changes_from_child(parent: Arc<Stack>, child: Stack) -> Stack {
103:         // we're going to drop the link to the parent stack on our new stack
104:         // so that we can unwrap the Arc as a unique reference
105:         drop(child.parent_stack);
106:         let mut unique_stack = Arc::unwrap_or_clone(parent);
107: 
108:         unique_stack
109:             .vars
110:             .retain(|(var, _)| !child.parent_deletions.contains(var));
111:         for (var, value) in child.vars {
112:             unique_stack.add_var(var, value);
113:         }
114:         unique_stack.env_vars = child.env_vars;
115:         unique_stack.env_hidden = child.env_hidden;
116:         unique_stack.active_overlays = child.active_overlays;
117:         unique_stack
118:     }

part.text:
Fixed. The issue was that child processes spawned via `run-external` inherited the parent OS process's full environment (std::process::Command inherits it by default), so variables hidden with `hide-env` — which are only removed from Nushell's internal environment — still leaked to children.

The fix in `crates/nu-command/src/system/run_external.rs:589` calls `process.env_clear()` before `process.envs(&self.env_vars)`, so child processes receive exactly Nushell's current (non-hidden) environment, matching the upstream fix.

Verified:
- `hides_environment_from_child` (the FAIL_TO_PASS case) now passes
- 168 tests in `shell::environment::env`, `repl::test_hiding`, and `shell::pipeline::commands::internal` pass
- 81 `overlays::` tests pass
